speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Mr Chairman, MOT looks after three connections of Singapore – sea, land and air.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The seaport and airport, as I have described before, are like the lungs of the country.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They draw in oxygen from the global eco-system, vitalising the rest of the Singapore economy.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Land transport is like the arteries and vessels, providing mobility for each of us as we work, live and play across the island.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Today, my colleagues and I will update the House on key long-term challenges and developments of our three connections.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The fortunes of a port city rise and fall.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Singapore suffered over three centuries of oblivion from the start of the 15th century.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, our status as a global transshipment hub today is not a right of birth but an earned and constant struggle for relevance.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Fortunately, our maritime sector has been resilient throughout COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, we are cautiously optimistic that we will have a good year in 2021.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But we had to make difficult decisions to get here.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Every day, more than 250 ships call at Singapore to deliver and transship cargo, for bunkering and repairs.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: While they are here, many ships want to change their crew who have been out at sea for several months.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: When the pandemic hit, crew change came to a halt because of border restrictions.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Seafarers on the vessels cannot disembark and new crew cannot fly in to board the vessels.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The shipping community faced a looming humanitarian crisis – hundreds of thousands of seafarers were stuck, stranded on board their work vessels, sometimes for more than a year.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, shipping lines urged Singapore, as a major transshipment port, to do something.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But to allow crew change in Singapore will expose ourselves to the risk of COVID-19 infections.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: If we wanted to be absolutely safe, we would have said "no", as many countries had.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But that would have turned our backs against the international maritime community.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They would have lost faith in us and it would have damaged our standing as a maritime hub.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Therefore, together with the industry and unions, we devised rigorous protocols to do crew change safely – repeated testing, quarantine, bubble wrap travel between the vessel and the hotel and the airport, and vice versa.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Our practice has been held up as an example at the International Maritime Organization (IMO).

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: As at end February 2021, we had eight imported cases due to crew change for ocean-going ships – very sorry to the Minister for Health – but none led to community infections.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: For some, they feel that it is more important to eliminate the virus from Singapore altogether.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But I think we did the right thing.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: For a city state like Singapore, the fight against COVID-19 is not about eliminating all risks by isolating ourselves.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It is about how to keep our connectivity open, supplies flowing, protecting jobs and our economy while keeping Singapore safe.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This is the real challenge of COVID-19 – not all-or-nothing, black-or-white, but the ability to navigate safely in a grey zone.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The Arctic route, the possibility of a Kra Canal and competition from neighbouring ports will continue to challenge our maritime relevance.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Senior Minister of State Chee Hong Tat will speak more about this.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I spoke about Electric Vehicles (EVs) but EVs are, at most, a second-best solution.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The cleanest and most sustainable way to move is still by mass public transport – buses and trains.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Over the last 10 years, it has increased almost by 10%.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Between now and 2025, we will progressively open the rest of the Thomson-East Coast Line.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: By 2026, we will "close the loop" for the Circle Line between Harbourfront and Marina Bay.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: By 2029, the Jurong Region Line will be completed.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In the 2030s, the Cross-Island Line will open progressively.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In that process, in response to Mr Melvin Yong, many jobs will be created.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: By then, our network density will be comparable to London and New York City.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: As suggested by Mr Melvin Yong and Mr Gan Thiam Poh, we will use technology wherever we can – big data to optimise routing and scheduling, sensors to carry out preventive maintenance effectively, kaizen projects to improve productivity and apps to help commuters plan for their trips.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: As for the men and women on the street, we will bring buses and trains as close as possible to their final destinations and also their origins, with pedestrian pathways and covered linkways wherever it makes sense.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: For short trips, you will notice commuters are increasingly either walking or cycling.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: That is why we are expanding the cycling network and repurposing roads wherever possible.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: LTA has identified 60 projects to convert suitable roads into footpaths, cycling paths or bus lanes.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Each project, we reckon, will have their pluses and minuses.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, for every project, we will work closely with the community and proceed only when we assess that, on balance, it benefits commuters and benefits the community.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I do not expect all 60 projects to proceed but we will learn from each experiment.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Senior Minister of State Amy Khor and Senior Parliamentary Secretary Baey Yam Keng will elaborate.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Several Members have shared their concerns on this and I appreciate Mr Saktiandi for especially highlighting this aspect of sustainability.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: What worries us more is whether we can afford the operating costs year after year on a long-term basis.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This includes manpower, energy, maintenance and renewal of operating assets like trains and signalling systems.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The Government needs to continue to subsidise the operations of MRT and buses.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I think we cannot run away from that.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But the bill to taxpayers cannot keep ballooning.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: If it does, we would leave our future generations a growing financial burden.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: For buses, we have settled on a bus contracting model that leverages competition to enhance the efficiency of operations.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: For MRT, we fully transited to the New Rail Financing Framework (NRFF) – mentioned by Mr Ang Wei Neng – a few years ago.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Under the first version of NRFF, the Government takes over from the transport operator the ownership and replacement of operating assets – trains and signalling systems.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The Government then charges the transport operator a fee for using these assets.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, it is like renting, on the part of the operator.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Under NRFF Version One, which was implemented for the Downtown Line (DTL), the operator pays a fixed fee, like a rental.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The public transport operator of the DTL still bears significant commercial risk.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: If ridership is healthy and fare revenue far exceeds operating cost, they get to enjoy a good part of the profit.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But if the reverse is true, they suffer losses.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This was not ideal because, as a public utility, public transport should be a more stable business.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, we adjusted the NRFF to reduce commercial volatility.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: If the operator enjoys high profits, the Government will cream off.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: If the operator suffers big losses, the Government cushions it.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, this is NRFF Version Two, implemented in 2016 to the North-South, East-West, Circle and North East Lines.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: For the most recent Thomson-East Coast Line (TEL), we took on another approach.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: For the initial period when ridership is still not stable, the Government collects all the fare revenue, bears all revenue risks and grants the operator a fee to run the line.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, it is a bit like a contracting model.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: After ridership stabilises, we revert to NRFF Version Two.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This will be done with a view to ensure that the operator will run the line reliably, with high productivity and that the line is sustainable.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: There are other things we need to do to keep our public transport system sustainable for the long run.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: First, operators must train their workers well and find new ways to be cost-efficient.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This includes keeping train services reliable and not trying to penny-pinch on maintenance cost, thinking that this will translate to savings and productivity.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This is needed as costs do go up, including the wages of public transport workers who look forward to earning more.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The Public Transport Council (PTC) makes a careful decision on fares every year.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Whenever there needs to be a fare adjustment, we will help lower income households through Public Transport Vouchers.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We also have fare concessions to large groups, such seniors and also young students.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: To the suggestion that maybe we should also extend this to adults taking courses, I would prefer to be very careful about it because, after all, all of us are going to be lifelong learners.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Third, we need to try to reduce excess capacity.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The majority of our bus services are trunk services.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: And they provide connection for commuters between towns.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, it has never been a pure hub-and-spoke system, as mentioned by Mr Melvin Yong and Mr Gan Thiam Poh.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: There will always be a core set of trunk services for buses.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But we should also try our best to reduce excess capacity in the system.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This is especially when new train lines come up, and ridership for bus services that run in parallel plunge, and then chalk up tens of millions of operating subsidies per service per year.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, we need to progressively adjust these bus services to better keep subsidies in check.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I used to be a union leader for the transport workers' union, and bus drivers on these services would always lament that 很心痛，载空气, they say in Chinese.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In English, it means when there are no passengers, it is a bit of a heartache, because they are just ferrying air.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Fourth, COVID-19 has also opened up an opportunity for us to make the system more efficient, by making the morning and evening peaks less pronounced.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: And to achieve this, we will need the co-operation of employers, to stagger working hours, allow working from home even after COVID-19 passes.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Almost a year later, the good news is Changi is now carrying five times that.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The bad news is, that works out to only 2.5% of pre-COVID 19 volume.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Flight movements look better, it is one quarter of pre-COVID-19 levels.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But this is, to a large extent, due to a larger number of cargo flights.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We expect connections to expand further in the coming months to about 80 cities.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In response to Mr Melvin Yong and Mr Dennis Tan, in a crisis like this, job prospects in the sector are naturally muted and subdued.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: About 500 are retrenchments, and the rest non-renewal of contracts or early retirement.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Non-residents shouldered the great majority of the reduction.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Hiring of graduates, asked by Mr Dennis Tan, have slowed, though there is still good demand for technicians coming out of our ITE, coming out of our Polytechnics.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I then checked with our Universities, who told me that most aerospace graduates still found jobs this year, but likely in non-aviation sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, fortunately, engineers are a very versatile bunch.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Mr Dennis Tan asked about help for the aerospace sector.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: There are three areas of help, and this was covered in the Budget Statement.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They also enjoy the Enhanced Training Support Package which provides stronger support when they send their workers for training.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Thousands have gone and it has been very helpful for the aerospace sector.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: And also, EDB put in a lot of effort to temporarily redeploy talents to other sectors while the sector waits for recovery.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Mr Dennis Tan asked what proportion of workers benefited from the COVID-19 related grants?

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I will say everyone who kept their jobs.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: That is the impact of the Jobs Support Scheme and the	Enhanced Training Support Package.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It helped all these companies stay above water, and retain core capabilities so that there is still a future for the sector.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: And that strategic outcome is either there or not there, either you believe it will work or you do not believe it will work, and you decide to do not do.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Ms Poh Li San asked how MOT plans to revive the aviation hub.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Unfortunately, I cannot answer that question with certainty.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We may have a plan, but this virus has no plan and it does not observe any rules.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It is driven by an instinct to dominate the world.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: To do so, it is transmitting without symptoms, and it is mutating.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, in terms of prospects, I can only say this: first, this year I do not think it is realistic to expect a V-shape recovery for the aviation sector.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Second, it is also possible that the virus becomes endemic, meaning it is something we have to live with, to cope with and to adapt to in the long term, just like the influenza virus.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: And third, notwithstanding this, with vaccines, and the realisation of governments around the world that they cannot perpetually close up their borders, I believe there will be some re-opening of borders this year, and some recovery this year.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, our mission this year is not so much to force a sharp recovery of the aviation sector, but to adapt to a new normal, to re-open safely, to build up confidence, to test workable concepts and to strengthen the belief that Changi Airport will still be an international air hub post-COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: And we are seeing signs of that happening.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: When WHO scientists from around the world were planning their study visit to Wuhan, they decided to gather in Singapore before they made their way, and they flew through Changi.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The World Economic Forum has decided to hold its meeting in Singapore, in August.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: A few months ago, a group of Vietnamese trainees going to Japan to complete their apprenticeship, decided to come to Singapore first and then up to Japan.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It is a longer route, but I think they like to fly SIA.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, the key question is: what are the steps we can take to re-open safely?

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: As I explained to the House before, what kills travel is quarantine and Stay-Home Notices (SHN).

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Very few people will want to travel abroad if they know they have to go through a lengthy isolation.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, to revive aviation, we need to replace quarantine and SHN with other methods that can also substantially mitigate the risk of transmission.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Now, I think there are four ways after all these months of experience.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The first is testing, which is key to re-opening borders.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: And with tests, we can detect infections early and prevent transmissions.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Ensure that they are kept to a tight itinerary, restricted premises, away from community, do not see anybody in the community.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This is how we managed to do maritime crew change and this is how the new Connect@Changi facility works.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The third is to recognise that travellers from certain places are safe, because they have successfully controlled the virus.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: That is why we unilaterally opened our borders to places such as Australia, New Zealand, Brunei and China.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: And so far, the scheme has not led to any increase in our local transmission.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: If other places reciprocate what we do, we have an Air Travel Bubble (ATB).

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In fact, I think ATBs are going to be important, which I will explain.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: And that leads to the fourth way, which is a new critical development – and that is vaccinations.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: It will require a system of certification, like the yellow booklet, which some of us have, that records our vaccinations against Malaria or Yellow Fever.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: And these discussions are happening bilaterally and also at the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO).

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: And Singapore, we have been active in all these discussions.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, this lung needs inflating, but our head is under water.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But each of these four methods I mentioned earlier are like snorkels, sticking out of the surface of the water.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They allow us to take in some oxygen, to keep Changi and to keep SIA going.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Because as vaccinations bring down infections across the world, more countries will be prepared to forge ATBs.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We can also identify places from low to moderate infection rates, and combine vaccination with tests, even "bubble wrap" travel, and to open up travel corridors.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: We will do our best to make all these arrangements bilateral so Singaporeans can travel outwards too.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Mr Chairman, COVID-19 has claimed many casualties: lives, careers, years of hard work wiped out in months.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Amongst them are notable brands – like Dan Ryans, like Robinsons.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I think we can get over the loss of these names.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But if we lose SIA or we lose Changi Airport, life in Singapore will never be quite the same.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The transport community knows this and what is at stake.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: On the first day of Chinese New Year, I joined the Prime Minister to send off three SIA flights.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: A cabin crew member I met told me she was issued quarantine orders three times, each time because she served somebody who later tested positive.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Fortunately, the last one was rescinded, so she served two.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: But each time she emerged from quarantine, she was just as passionate about flying.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: When we rolled out vaccination for maritime and aviation frontliners, the workers turned out in force.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In the coming days, I think we will cross 90% for both doses as well.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I recently met a resident in my constituency.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: He greeted me warmly and gave me a fist bump.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: He told me he is a maritime worker, he said, "I have gotten vaccinated.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I can now protect my family." Crowne Plaza is our airport hotel, housing foreign air crew laying over in Singapore for one, two days.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Unfortunately, there were transmissions in the hotel, three workers, local workers, got infected.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The General Manager and executives rolled up their sleeves, went to the kitchen, took over the kitchen operations.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: I hope the food tasted okay that day.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: They closed the hotel after that for a month, tightened the procedures.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Week in week out, I see for myself the fight in our workers at our borders.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Mr Chairman, I have told the tale of our three connections.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: On the seas, we learn to adapt, find the courage and humanity within us to take reasonable risks and to be of service to the world.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: On the roads, we will need to be greener, more sustainable – in both the way we travel, and the way we fund our infrastructure.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: In aviation, it is the battle of our lifetime, and a story about our spirit of resilience – to press on with duties despite rounds of quarantine; of fortitude – to answer the call to be vaccinated to protect family and nation; of never-say-die – rolling up our sleeves and doing the hard work when duty calls.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: So, on the revival of aviation, I do not have a water-tight and detailed plan to present to the House, one that meets the much-vaunted high standards of our Civil Service.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: Instead, we can only be guided by an unfailing drive to keep pushing forward, knowing that for every two steps we move forward, we may have to take a step back, sometimes, two steps back, and knowing that if we are too reckless and ambitious and take too big a leap, we may have to be set back by a mile.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: With each setback, we and I will be questioned, "Why do you even bother with such an idea?

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: The worst thing to do now is not even try, because that is giving up the fight.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
text: This is what we need most, perhaps as importantly as vaccines, to not just walk, run, ride, cycle, sail – but to fly and to soar into the skies again.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Mr Chairman, I will speak about growing our maritime sector and LTA's pro-enterprise efforts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Our International Maritime Centre grew in scale and diversity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We attracted 11 new shipping groups to Singapore and worked with eight maritime companies to expand their operations here.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat asked about growing the maritime sector and creating jobs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We must not be too satisfied with our success to become complacent.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We will build on the momentum and seize new opportunities to create an integrated, innovative and inclusive Maritime Singapore eco-system – what we call the three "I"s.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Our port is consistently ranked first or second in the world on efficiency, reliability and connectivity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: If we do not stay ahead of the competition, others will steal our lunch.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We must continue to differentiate ourselves and bring value to our customers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We are consolidating all of PSA's operations from Pasir Panjang, Keppel and Brani into one integrated Tuas Port, what the Prime Minister called "our next bold move".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: This additional capacity will allow PSA to serve more ships and further enhance our network connectivity, which is a critical factor for a transshipment hub port.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Tuas Port will offer best-in-class efficiency, productivity, reliability and sustainability.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: It will be fully automated – from cranes to driverless vehicles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: These will more than double our labour productivity at Tuas, compared to our City Terminals, and create many skilled jobs for Singaporeans in the port sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: It will also be a greener port, with a 50% reduction in carbon emissions intensity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The concept of integration extends beyond the port.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: To key sectors like advanced manufacturing, cold chain and logistics, which form the Tuas Port eco-system, we can move containers directly from the ships to the factories without additional delays or handling costs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We are also enhancing digital integration to facilitate data exchange, helping companies to enjoy greater convenience, reduce costs and save time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Mr Ang Wei Neng asked about accessibility and housing for workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We plan to develop Tuas South region for industrial use over the next two decades.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We will continue to explore viable transport options for workers and work with MND to increase public housing options in the West.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We will partner and support maritime technology SMEs: to push research and technology boundaries; scale up and team up; and turn challenges into new opportunities for growth.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We will increase the cap of co-funding support for maritime technology SMEs from 50% currently to 70%, and encourage industry players to share expertise and resources to co-develop scalable solutions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Eligible projects by industry consortiums will also receive up to 70% co-funding support.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: In total, we will have $100 million to fund maritime R&D and product development.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We aim to more than triple the number of maritime tech start-ups supported under the PIER71 funding programme from 30 to 100 by 2025.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The start-up eco-system is gaining momentum with wider industry support.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Recently, SEEDS Capital partnered venture development firms to co-invest up to $50 million into maritime technology start-ups.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Our goal is to be the top maritime start-up hub in the world, the Silicon Valley for maritime technology.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Mr Saktiandi asked about the Green Energy and Technology Programme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: A key project is the electrification of harbour craft.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Our call for proposals has received interest from 16 industry consortiums.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: MPA is also drawing up a Maritime Singapore Decarbonisation Blueprint 2050 together with the industry to promote sustainable practices and identify new job opportunities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: I have spoken about the first two "I"s, "integrated" and "innovative".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The third "I" is inclusive, which reflects our vision of creating a diverse range of jobs for Singaporeans with different backgrounds and skillsets.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We want to attract and train more Singaporeans to take on seafaring and shore-based jobs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: As the maritime sector grows and transforms, there will be new opportunities and new pathways in areas such as environmental sustainability, systems engineering, cybersecurity and data analytics.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: MPA is partnering the industry and Institutions of Higher Learning to facilitate training, attachment and traineeship opportunities as part of the SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The training allowances will increase from 1 April.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We are also encouraging maritime companies to tap on the Jobs Growth Incentive to increase local hiring as well as Professional Conversion Programmes for mid-career entrants.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Mr Saktiandi and Mr Ang Wei Neng asked about this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: LTA's work impacts businesses beyond the land transport sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The built environment sector is one example as development plans involving transport infrastructure or traffic flows require LTA's approval.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Companies often request LTA to expedite their approvals to reduce processing time and business costs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Companies also introduce new business models and technologies, including green solutions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: So, LTA's rules and regulations need to stay ahead of the curve to support new innovations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: At the same time, LTA is responsible for public safety and a pleasant commuting experience for all.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The panel will find ways to reduce business costs and improve efficiency.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: This win-win outcome can only be achieved if the industry is clear about what is required in the submissions, to avoid multiple back-and-forths.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: LTA will work with the professional bodies to conduct sessions and raise awareness on what is required for the submissions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: LTA is also working with URA and other agencies to better integrate transport and land use planning-related information.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: This will be uploaded online for public access when ready.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: It will reduce information gaps and facilitate more public-private collaborations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Some they will support, others, they will have to say no.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: It is not a free-for-all, but also not nothing at all.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: To try new ideas, we must also be prepared to take calculated risks and accept some failure along the way.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: This is why I support setting up regulatory sandboxes where necessary to pilot new technologies and business models.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: If the experiment fails, we limit the downsides, we learn from the experience and we try again.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: If it succeeds, we can scale up the idea and extend it to other areas across Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: This is what former Head of Civil Service, Mr Peter Ho, calls, "aiming for safe fail, rather than fail safe".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Mr Chairman, in the Summer Palace in Beijing, there was a stone boat built by Emperor Qianlong.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: He hoped the Qing Dynasty would be like the stone boat – unshakeable and unsinkable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: And we know what eventually happened to the Qing Dynasty.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: When we build ships, it is not to anchor them in the harbour or in some lake in the Summer Palace.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: It is to sail out to the oceans, to the open seas and reach new lands, including going into uncharted waters.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: To be an innovative nation, we must have the same pioneering spirit and sense of adventure like our forefathers: willing to leave our comfort zones and take calculated risks, never giving up when we encounter challenges and always looking to pursue new rainbows on the horizon.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: My speech will touch on how the land transport sector is coping with the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: I will share how we are future-proofing our land transport workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Then, I will explain how we will partner the community to repurpose stretches of roads for footpaths and cycling paths to enhance connectivity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: As the COVID-19 situation evolved, we had to implement additional safe management measures while ensuring that our transport operations continued to run smoothly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: On behalf of MOT, I applaud them for their courage, dedication and resilience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We are also grateful for the strong support by the unions, associations and transport operators.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: A good example is that of the taxi and private hire car (PHC) sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Right at the start of the pandemic, the Government worked closely with the National Taxi Association (NTA), the National Private Hire Vehicles Association (NPHVA) and the taxi and PHC operators to introduce the Special Relief Fund (SRF), which provided much needed support to our taxi and PHC drivers amidst a significant decline in ridership.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: In view of the fluid circumstances, we will continue to monitor the situation closely to assess if further support is necessary.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Mr Ang shared his concerns about young drivers in the taxi and PHC sector and asked if the Government will consider capping the number of PHCs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: From this group, those below 30 years old make up about 3% of all TDVL and PDVL holders, and they have been grandfathered.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: For example, we observed a 12% drop in the number of registered PHCs since the start of the pandemic.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: For drivers who exit the taxi and PHC sectors amidst the pandemic, we appreciate the Labour Movement’s assistance in helping them to upskill and look for alternative jobs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Last but not least, we have also partnered NTA, NPHVA and the taxi and PHC operators to commence vaccinations for taxi and PHC drivers last week.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This forms part of our efforts to offer vaccinations to our frontline land transport workers and strengthen the resilience of our essential services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Since last week, MOH has issued SMS notifications to all of the more than 50,000 active taxi and PHC drivers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: More than 50% of those invited have booked their vaccination appointments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will work with the associations and operators to encourage more drivers to get vaccinated.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The strong tripartite partnerships that have helped us weather the COVID-19 pandemic will also be critical to support the transformation of our workforce to meet longer term needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Before COVID-19, we were already looking into trends such as digitalisation and new vehicular technologies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: These present many challenges but also create exciting opportunities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: As Mr Melvin Yong pointed out, the electrification of the land transport system will create many jobs and opportunities for upskilling.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: New competencies are required to maintain EVs and charging infrastructure.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: In December 2020, the Government supported the establishment of the Singapore Motor Workshop Association’s training facility to impart EV-related competencies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will continue to work closely with companies, training providers and unions, to identify ways to support young graduates and existing workers to acquire such competencies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Ms Yeo also asked how we are helping taxi and PHC drivers cope with longer term technology developments, such as digitalisation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: LTA is engaging the industry on an updated training curriculum for the Taxi Driver’s and the PHC Driver’s Vocational Licences, which will place greater emphasis on key competencies to help drivers cope with digitalisation, such as mapping and navigational tools.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The new curriculum will also allow drivers to be kept up-to-date with new vehicular technology, such as electric and autonomous vehicles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: LTA will also support greater use of technology to train taxi and PHC drivers, by facilitating training centres to offer online TDVL refresher courses so that the drivers can attend the courses at their convenience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: A new conversion course will also be introduced to allow drivers to convert their PDVLs to TDVLs to expand the driving options for vocational drivers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: LTA will announce more details at a later date.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Beyond workforce transformation, we can also emerge stronger by building a more sustainable and inclusive transport system under the Singapore Green Plan 2030.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will encourage more people to switch from private vehicles to Walk, Cycle and Ride (WCR) modes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Since the start of the COVID-19 pandemic, many Singaporeans have embraced cycling and walking.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This is an important measure to prevent the import of non-compliant devices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Meanwhile, we will continue with regular inspections of AM devices to deter illegal modifications.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This will allow more cycling journeys to be completed entirely on the cycling path network, although cyclists may still have to dismount and push at certain locations, such as overhead bridges, for safety reasons.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will also prioritise construction for towns that do not have cycling paths.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Senior Parliamentary Secretary Baey will elaborate on how we will develop a culture of gracious usage on paths to complement these efforts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will also have transit priority corridors, to enhance the travel experience by public transport.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The North-South Corridor (NSC) is one such example.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: The NSC will also serve as a green thoroughfare from the North into the city centre with its cycling trunk routes and pedestrian paths.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Chairman, going forward, as Ms Yeo and Mr Lim have suggested, we will work closely with the community to develop AM infrastructure.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will repurpose suitable stretches of road into footpaths, cycling paths or bus lanes, and incorporate features that contribute to place making.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will seek views from residents, grassroots volunteers, Town Councils, and local businesses, to identify potential enhancements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: These views will shape key project details, such as the length of the stretch being repurposed, or when permanent infrastructure enhancement works will commence or even if the project should proceed at all.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will start with projects to enhance walkability, starting with areas such as the Civic District as Mr Cheng Hsing Yao has highlighted to benefit the widest spectrum of users.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Over the years, we have worked with arts and civic groups and premise owners to realise their aspirations for greater walkability within the Civic District.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We have pedestrianised one side of Anderson Bridge and part of St Andrew’s Road, and restricted vehicle access to stretches of Parliament Place, Old Parliament Lane and Connaught Drive.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: With this, pedestrians can walk seamlessly from Old Parliament House to Esplanade Park.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Many Singaporeans have expressed a desire for more extensive pedestrianisation of the Civic District.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: Mr Mok Wei Wei, the architect for the upgrading of the Victoria Theatre and Concert Hall, suggested fully pedestrianising Anderson Bridge as a gateway to the District.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: This would offer unblocked and panoramic views of the District’s architecture.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will consider his suggestion alongside others from visitors, arts and civic groups and premise owners, as we work towards our vision of a more pedestrian-friendly Civic District.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan)
text: We will start with a stretch of Havelock Road.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This is a mature estate, and we have heard residents and grassroots volunteers share their desire to make the road more walkable.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Chairman, 2020 was a difficult year for the land transport sector.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This will enable us to walk, cycle and ride safely and comfortably while we look to soar in the skies again!

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Chairman, I will share our efforts in building a transport system that is safe and inclusive for all, on public paths and public transport.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: More people are taking up cycling and other active modes, with monthly shared bike use tripling in 2020.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: It is important that all path users, both pedestrians and riders, remain safe.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Ms Yeo Wan Ling asked about improving path safety.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This will go some way towards one, ensuring the accident victims receive compensation and two, protecting commercial riders against excessive claims.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Ms Yeo Wan Ling and Mr Lim Biow Chuan asked about our efforts to educate pedestrians and riders.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: From May we will launch a new "Move Happy" Graciousness campaign to raise awareness on safe and gracious path-sharing with three guidelines: one, keep left on paths; second, use the most appropriate path; and third, be alert of our surroundings.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We have also run the Safe Riding Programme (SRP) since 2018.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Many participants found this voluntary session a fun and hands-on way to learn about safe riding.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: I am pleased to announce that we are refreshing the SRP around the second quarter this year to make it even more interactive.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Responsible behaviour is also important in keeping roads safe.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Like other road users, cyclists must follow traffic rules.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Motorists should look out for more vulnerable users.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: With the right mindset and a culture of graciousness, we can enjoy active mobility in a safe and harmonious way.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Chairman, allow me to say a few words in Mandarin.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: (In Mandarin):    A culture of graciousness is critical in making our public transport system safe and inclusive.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Taking the trains and buses is a big part of our daily lives.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: To able-bodied Singaporeans, the public transport system is an easy way to get around quickly and conveniently.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: But the commute can be a bit challenging for elderly and commuters with special needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: They, too, should be able to use public transport seamlessly and safely.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We can be more understanding towards this group of commuters, by putting their needs before ours, and stepping forward to help fellow commuters.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: These acts of care may be small, but they can really make a difference to those who need help.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Recently, Ang Mo Kio MRT station service ambassadors told me that students with autism from the nearby Pathlight School sometimes would look for them to have a chat.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: To these commuters with special needs, the familiar faces of the service ambassadors can be a source of comfort and encouragement.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: I have written a short poem to encourage everyone: "Pedestrians, cyclists and Personal Mobility Device riders, A friendly reminder to not rush, Please slow down when there is someone in front of you.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Do look at the road ahead and not at your phone.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Whether on the MRT or the bus, Do not neglect the culture of being a caring commuter.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Let us aim for a smooth travel without barriers, Everyone appreciates a gracious commute experience." (In English): Chairman, last year, I announced the setting up of a Caring SG Commuters Committee.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Ms Poh Li San asked about our plans.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Over the past year, the Committee engaged many commuters.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Through focus group discussions and surveys, the Committee found that Singaporeans want to help fellow commuters, but often do not know how.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Only about one in four commuters know how to assist commuters with conditions such as hearing and developmental disabilities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: I can understand why, because these conditions may not be immediately noticeable.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We will therefore try to help the public better understand other commuters’ needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: One key initiative is the recruitment of Caring Commuter Champions, who will be trained by SG Enable to support commuters with special needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: I hope more people will volunteer as Caring Commuter Champions, to make a change in your fellow commuters’ journeys.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The Public Transport Council also found that only around half of survey respondents were comfortable to ask for help even if they needed it.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: It is sometimes awkward to ask for help, especially when we do not want to inconvenience others.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We want to make it easier for commuters to ask for help.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: In October 2019, LTA launched a pilot where commuters who need a seat could alert others with a "May I have a seat please?” sticker.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Go-Ahead Singapore also launched a “Helping Hand” trial, providing commuters with mobility needs a card with instructions for the bus captains.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: From April, commuters with long-term, invisible medical conditions or disabilities can request for a specially designed card and lanyard at Passenger Service Centres and Offices.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The Government will continue to invest in safety and inclusivity-related initiatives.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We are improving accessibility for persons with disabilities, as Mr Gerald Giam has suggested.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Today, all train stations and bus interchanges are barrier-free.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: These are useful for commuters who may not see as well, or may not understand English.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: These will be rolled out to all new stations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: However, we need to prioritise our efforts given the high cost of infrastructural improvements.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: So, I seek Mr Gerald Giam’s and Mr Faisal Manap’s understanding that we must be financially prudent and focus on areas near transport nodes first.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Chairman, our daily commutes are not just about moving a person from one point to another.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: They are also about sharing and navigating a common space, on public paths and public transport.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We will continue to partner the community to achieve our vision of a safe and inclusive transport system for all.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: I have two clarifications: one for Senior Minister of State Amy Khor, and another clarification for Senior Minister of State Mr Chee Hong Tat.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: First for the maritime sector, we are very glad to hear that the Tuas Port will just not be a port but a hub.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: Activities would include a lot of supplementary industries.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: And we know that it could be the best in class, but I hope that it will be best in class supported by a best in class MRT station as well.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: I did not hear Senior Minister of State Chee Hong Tat saying anything about having a train connection there, but he mentioned about having a new housing estate.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: So, we hope that he can clarify, because by 2030, as what Minister said, there will still be no train to the Tuas Port area.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: The second clarification is for Senior Minister of State Amy Khor.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: Did I hear correctly that we will add 28 km of cycling path by the end of the year?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: If so, it does not seem very exciting.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: For example, in Nanyang estate, there are a lot of cyclists, but there are zero cycling paths, zero kilometers of cycling path.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: So, what does it take to double or triple the building of cycling paths this year and next, rather than wait for a longer time?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Mr Chairman, in my speech earlier, I mentioned for the Tuas Port, that we will continue to explore viable transport options for workers.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, this is something which we will study and Mr Ang is right that if you look at the demand for transport connectivity to that part of Singapore, it will not only depend on the Tuas Port alone but also what are the other developments in the surrounding area using the port as a key hub supporting the growth of different industries.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Those are the completed cycling paths that we will be adding on.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Many of these, you can look into not just pedestrianising, adding footpaths, but perhaps widening it for cycling paths.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Whether if these can come aboard really depends on the support from the local community.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: When we do road repurposing projects, we have to work very closely with the local community to see if this is something they would support.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: When you do this, there will be some trade-offs.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For instance, the benefits may take time to come, but the immediate impact is on motorists.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: They will probably have to divert the roads if we pedestrianise or we widen the cycling paths.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: They may have to park somewhere else, for instance, if we include the cycling paths.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, we have to look at how to minimise the inconvenience and at the same time, look at how we can bring benefits to the community and look at how to mitigate some of the trade-offs.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Actually, I did say in my speech that we will especially focus on those towns where there are no cycling paths.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, if the Member is keen on this, let us look at it.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: Mr Chairman, fortunately I am not asking for cycling paths for Toa Payoh, as we already have those, and we are thankful to MOT for the cycling paths there.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: I have two questions, Mr Chairman, one to Minister and second to Senior Minister of State Chee.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: My question is with regard to fare concessions.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: The last fare concession increase, if we look at MOT's website, the last inclusion into the fare concession coverage was in 2019, where PTC extended student concessionary fares to Polytechnics and other diploma students.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: And I think it benefited more than 80,000.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: My question is, are there any new concessions in play going forward, in future as fare adjustments come on stream.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: And the Minister highlighted that fare increases might come in going forward, and what are the plans in terms of concessions?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: The reason why I highlighted about the adult learners, is to capture some elements of adult learners who are studying in the Polytechnics.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: Some may not be captured in the move on 2019.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: The second question is with regard to Mr Chee's response just now, the seafaring and shore-based jobs, and the green maritime sector jobs.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: How many jobs will be created in those sectors?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: And whether more can be done to entice more Singaporeans, young Singaporeans, to explore good jobs there?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: I think not many of our young or our Singaporeans are aware of some of these jobs there.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: I think those are good jobs that we need to let them know even more about going forward.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I want to assure Mr Saktiandi, I really understand what you are saying.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: In 2019, in fact, I was really happy that fare concession was extended to Polytechnic students, because the then Minister for Education lobbied very hard for it.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And the then Minister for Transport was kind enough to also support it.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But I think going beyond that, it becomes less obvious.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And I think we keep to that principle and see how we can best ensure that those who find difficulty affording can be protected against fare increases.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Mr Chairman, I think Mr Saktiandi asked a very important question about jobs, because when we pursue growth, when we attract investments, what is the end in mind?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: One very important objective is to create good jobs for our people.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: In the maritime sector, our aim is to be able to create an inclusive and diverse range of jobs.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: When we pursue environmental sustainability, green growth, de-carbonisation of shipping and port operations, I think this will open up new opportunities and new possibilities.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: All that will create a lot of opportunities for different groups of Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Young graduates, but also mid-career entrants who want to join the sector.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I think in the process of doing so, together with growth, we are then able to provide higher pay, better prospects, and I think this will allow us to attract more Singaporeans to enter the sector.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: First, I would like to thank the Minister and all the appointment holders for the answers that they have given in the Committee of Supply.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: The first question I have is in respect of what Senior Parliamentary Secretary Baey has shared with us regarding safe riding.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: I agree with Member Ms Yeo Wan Ling's concern regarding safe riding on footpaths.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: I think it is a message that I have shared virtually every year in the last couple of years.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: Yesterday, I shared during the MND Committee of Supply in a cut on safety of the Park Connector Network (PCN).

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: The reason why I shared during the MND Committee of Supply – but it is related to, I think, a lot on LTA's efforts on this – is that I believe that a busy PCN, especially during peak times, is always a good indicator of the state of our culture of path sharing by different users.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: I expressed concern that over two years because – I shared a previous cut on this two years ago in the same MND Committee of Supply – I felt that there is not many changes in terms of the culture.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: Therefore, I would like to implore LTA to continue to work on public education as well as consistent enforcement.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: I appreciate Senior Parliamentary Secretary Baey sharing about the efforts.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: Can I continue to implore LTA to consider public education from the point of view of not just giving information to interested users who will draw information from the Facebook but rather to think about how to disseminate public education on safe and considerate use of footpaths and the PCN, to people who do not consciously look for it.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: Because these are people who use our footpaths, the aunties and uncles who may get upset with people ringing the bell when cyclists are passing by, keeping left or keeping right, people walking their dogs on the PCN or footpaths, stopping to chat.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: My third clarification is not really a clarification but I would like to take the opportunity to thank the Minister for sharing about crew change.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: I do not have a clarification because I filed a Parliamentary Question on this recently and I would like to thank the Minister and the Senior Minister of State, perhaps, for a very comprehensive answer on my Parliamentary Question on NewOcean 6, relating to the measures on crew change arising from the infection of crew on visiting ships to the port of Singapore.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: I just want to take the opportunity to applaud the hard work and the good efforts of MOT and MPA on coming up with the crew change policies and guidelines, as well as for safe boarding of visiting vessels at the port of Singapore by workmen or third parties.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: I think it is a lot of hard work and I agree with the Minister, and as a member of the maritime community, I agree that these efforts are very important to continue in this COVID-19 climate.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: It is very important for our port of Singapore, our businesses and our reputation.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: So, I would like to thank MPA and MOT officers for their hard work.

speaker: The Chairman
text: The guillotine time is 2.10 pm, so let us try to finish by then.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: In the interest of time, I will answer all three.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We will take them in but as he says, culture change is not easy, it takes time.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Step by step, we will move in the right direction.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I do want to make a clarification in my speech just now.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I mentioned some retrenchment figures and reduction in labour force figures.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And again, very much borne by the foreign workforce.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I must place on record our thanks to MOH, who worked side by side with us to make this possible.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: There are many ministries of health in the world who just want total elimination of viruses.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But I think we had a good relationship working with MOH.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: You take a big deep breath and say, "Let's make this step"; put in the safety precautions, work with the industry and all the stakeholders, plus the healthcare professionals and experts.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Saktiandi, would you like to withdraw your amendment?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: Mr Chairman, we have been discussing about the lifeblood and lungs of Singapore over the past two hours.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: The Minister even talked about snorkeling underwater to fill our lungs with much needed oxygen and even spoke about taking a deep breath just now!

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: But it has been an extremely challenging time for the transport sector, especially with the sharp drop in air travel, commuter volumes and connectivity for the past months.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: The stakes are high as the pandemic is still fraught with uncertainties.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: It is also challenging to determine the new travel patterns of the near future.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: But there are exciting times ahead, from the responses just now, for our land transport sector and efforts are being made to make sure our air and sea hubs will thrive again.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: And most importantly, our transport frontliners, for their hard work, conviction and passion to keep our air and sea hubs, and land transport systems running efficiently, smoothly and safely, day and night, since COVID-19 hit us, and also to be ready for the future.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: With that, Mr Chairman, I beg leave to withdraw my amendment.

speaker: The Chairman
text: With COVID-19 still around, do be careful how you take your deep breath.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Make sure you are masked when you are doing it.
